issues.description: Core.NamespaceSealed is a stub returning false unconditionally while already wired into security-relevant call sites
issues.detail: (*Core).NamespaceSealed returns false with a TODO and is already consumed by ListAllNamespaces and root-token paths. A predicate central to access-control safety committed in a state where its negative branch cannot fire is a load-bearing lie: callers will silently treat sealed namespaces as unsealed, and there is no compile-time guarantee downstream code gets updated when SealManager lands. Either gate it behind a build tag / return ErrNotImplemented / panic, change the signature to (bool, error), or do not merge until SealManager exists. A TODO is not a contract.

issues.description: ACL root authorization now hinges on ns.HasParent(a.root) with unspecified semantics and no test coverage of the dangerous directions
issues.detail: AllowOperation's new fast-path reads `if !ns.HasParent(a.root) { return ret }` then grants RootPrivs. The direction matters: is it 'a.root is an ancestor of ns' (root policy from parent grants in child) or the reverse (catastrophic)? Is HasParent reflexive? The test only covers same-namespace cases plus one negative; siblings, cousins, deeper descendants, root-policy-from-child, and the identity case are unexercised. State the invariant and the HasParent contract in code, capture rootNamespaceID/path as a value rather than a mutable pointer identity, and add table-driven tests for every ancestry case before this can ship.

issues.description: ACL.root field overloads 'is root policy' and 'which namespace owns the root scope' in a single nilable pointer
issues.detail: The field flipped from a clean bool to *namespace.Namespace, encoding both the predicate ('is this ACL root?') and identity ('which namespace?') in one nullable value. Readers must know the convention 'nil means not-root, non-nil means root scoped to this ns'. Decompose into explicit fields (isRoot bool + rootNamespace *Namespace), or wrap in a small named type with a stated contract and accessor methods (IsRoot, RootNamespace). The current shape forces every reader of the struct to reconstruct the invariant from construction logic in NewACL.

issues.description: Removed 'root policy only allowed in root namespace' invariant in NewACL with no stated replacement gate
issues.detail: Previously NewACL refused a root-named policy outside the root namespace. The diff removes the guard and silently records whatever namespace is on the context as the root scope. The system-wide invariant 'only the root namespace can grant root privileges' is now replaced by 'whatever namespace was in context when NewACL was called', with no exhibited proof that all NewACL callers validate the principal's authority to mint such a policy. Either restore the guard until the upstream check exists, or document the new precondition on NewACL and enumerate the call sites that establish it.

issues.description: AdjustErrorStatusCode if-chain to switch refactor silently changes precedence semantics
issues.detail: The previous code was a sequence of independent if-statements where multiple branches could fire and later assignments (notably the HTTPCodedError passthrough) overrode earlier ones. The new switch short-circuits on first match: an error that both wraps ErrSealed and implements HTTPCodedError now locks in 503 instead of honoring the coded status. This is a behavioral change disguised as a cleanup. Either preserve the original sequential semantics, or document and test the new precedence explicitly.

issues.description: ErrNamespaceSealed detection uses fragile errwrap.Contains string matching instead of errors.Is
issues.detail: `errwrap.Contains(err, consts.ErrNamespaceSealed.Error())` matches by substring on a short, generic message ('namespace is sealed') — any wrapped error whose text happens to contain that string will be downgraded to 503. With two sealed-error sentinels now in play, the chance of cross-contamination grows. Prefer errors.Is on a wrapped sentinel; the new sentinel is the moment to switch, not to propagate the legacy pattern.

issues.description: NSTokenLength = TokenLen + "."[1] + nsID is cryptic and likely wrong as written
issues.detail: The expression indexes past the end of a one-byte string literal (or sums an integer with the ASCII byte value 46) instead of expressing 'one separator byte'. Either it is a typo for len(".") (=1) or compile-time obfuscation; either way `TokenLen + 1 + NamespaceIDLen` with a named separator constant and a documented token layout (`<token>.<nsID>`) is obvious. Define the codec (encode/decode functions returning (token, nsID, error)) and derive the length from those — don't smuggle structure into an arithmetic constant.

issues.description: PR mixes three independent changes — ACL semantics flip, sealed-namespace scaffolding, and mass test churn
issues.detail: The patch combines (1) the load-bearing ACL root refactor, (2) the ErrNamespaceSealed sentinel plus Core.NamespaceSealed stub plus ListAllNamespaces contract change, and (3) hundreds of lines of mechanical context.Background() → namespace.RootContext(t.Context()) rewrites. Mashed together, the test churn hides the four lines in acl.go that actually change security behavior. Split into independently reviewable patches so the ACL change is auditable on its own and git bisect remains useful.

issues.description: ListAllNamespaces contract change (now includes sealed namespaces) and migration to c.ListNamespaces is undocumented at call sites
issues.detail: Four call sites in core.go, core_metrics.go, and counters.go switched from `c.namespaceStore.ListAllNamespaces(ctx, true)` to `c.ListNamespaces(ctx)`. The explicit `true` parameter (include sealed) is now hidden inside the wrapper, and the postcondition delta affects MFA enforcement, locked-user updates, entity gauges, and active token counting — each of which has a different correct answer for 'include sealed?'. Write the contract on ListNamespaces and ListAllNamespaces, and justify per call site whether including sealed namespaces is the intended behavior. Consider naming the wrapper to make the policy explicit at call sites.

issues.description: leaseView / tokenIndexView lose the root-namespace branch without a documented equivalence assertion
issues.detail: ExpirationManager.leaseView and tokenIndexView previously branched on ns.ID == RootNamespaceID, using systemBarrierView.SubView(...) for root and namespaceMountEntryView for child namespaces. The diff unifies both into NamespaceView(m.core.barrier, ns).SubView(...). For this to be a pure refactor, NamespaceView(barrier, RootNamespace).SubView(prefix) must produce byte-identical storage keys to the old root path; if it differs by one byte, every existing root-namespace lease becomes unreachable post-upgrade. Add a migration test or invariant comment asserting the equivalence.

issues.description: Comment on a.root field is imprecise and the field is mis-named for its load-bearing role
issues.detail: The comment ('root property is a non-nil namespace if the "root" named policy (and only "root") is present') doesn't state the ancestry rule that decides authorization, and doesn't precisely capture the iff condition. Rename the field to rootNamespace or rootPolicyNS so the type and intent are self-documenting, and rewrite the comment to state: non-nil iff the policy set is exactly {root}; when non-nil it identifies the namespace in which the policy was instantiated, and a request in namespace ns is root-allowed iff ns.HasParent(rootNamespace).

issues.description: Repetitive namespace.RootContext(t.Context()) test plumbing could be a one-line helper
issues.detail: Roughly 30+ test sites mechanically replace context.Background() / namespace.RootContext(nil) with namespace.RootContext(t.Context()). A small helper (testRootCtx(t) or table-level setup) would shrink the diff and reduce future churn. Worth considering whether functions that require a namespace should take it as an explicit parameter rather than smuggling it through context — but at minimum, factor the repetition.

synthesis.summary: Panel consensus: REFUSE as written. Two P0s are load-bearing and security-critical: (1) Core.NamespaceSealed is a stub returning false unconditionally while ListAllNamespaces and root-token paths already consume it as fact — flagged unanimously by all six reviewers; (2) the ACL root fast-path was rewritten to depend on ns.HasParent(a.root) without stated semantics, without test coverage of siblings/cousins/identity/grandchild cases, and with the prior 'root policy only in root namespace' invariant silently removed. A third P0 is structural: ACL.root flipped from bool to *namespace.Namespace, conflating 'is root' with 'which namespace' in a nilable pointer. P1s include a silent precedence change in the if-chain-to-switch refactor of AdjustErrorStatusCode, fragile errwrap.Contains substring matching for the new sealed sentinel, a likely-broken NSTokenLength expression, undocumented ListAllNamespaces contract change, and mixing three independent patches into one. Recommend splitting the PR, restoring or replacing the NewACL guard, stating contracts on NamespaceSealed/HasParent/ListAllNamespaces/ACL.root, and adding table-driven ancestry tests before merge.
